_comment: F350. The evidence set behind SemanticRanker.minimumSimilarity and RankFusion.k, which
until now lived in one session's shell history and could not be re-derived.
Wholly invented. No user meeting, recording or transcript was read to build it (AGENTS.md).
Every question is a PARAPHRASE of its passage, sharing as few content words with it as a
natural phrasing allows. That is the point: a question that repeats the passage's own words
is answered by BM25 alone and measures nothing about search by meaning. It also means the
keyword-only recall reported by the scorer is expected to be LOW — that is the baseline the
semantic half has to beat, not a defect.

meetings.title: Pricing review
segments: Let us start with where the tiers landed after last quarter's feedback.
We are moving the starter plan from nineteen dollars to twenty-nine a month.
Anyone already on the old rate keeps it for twelve months, no exceptions.
The enterprise tier stays negotiated, so nothing changes for those accounts.
Support wants a week of lead time before the page goes live.
I will draft the email to existing customers by Thursday.
We should expect some churn in the first month and plan for it.
Next item is the renewal dashboard nobody has looked at since June.

meetings.title: Hiring sync
segments: Three candidates finished the on-site loop this week.
The backend role has been open for four months now, which is too long.
We are losing people at the take-home stage because it takes six hours.
Let us cut the exercise down to ninety minutes and see if that helps.
Referrals convert twice as often as inbound applications do.
I want a written scorecard before anyone debriefs out loud.
Budget approves two more headcount for the second half of the year.
The intern programme starts in June and needs mentors assigned.

meetings.title: Incident postmortem
segments: The outage began at 03:12 and lasted just under forty minutes.
A configuration push removed the read replica from the pool.
Nobody was paged because the alert routed to a rotation that had ended.
Customers saw timeouts on checkout but no data was lost.
We are adding a staging soak of thirty minutes before any pool change.
The on-call schedule will be validated automatically every morning.
I do not want to blame the person who ran the push; the guardrail was missing.
Follow-up items are due before the end of the sprint.

meetings.title: Roadmap planning
segments: We have committed to offline mode for the autumn release.
Search is the single most requested thing in the feedback inbox.
The mobile rewrite slips to next year; there is no way around it.
Two engineers move to the integrations team starting Monday.
Anything not on this list is explicitly not happening this half.
We will review scope again after the design review in three weeks.
Marketing needs six weeks of notice before any launch date is public.
Let us keep one slot free for whatever the incident review turns up.

meetings.title: Design review
segments: The new onboarding drops from nine screens to four.
People abandon at the permissions step more than anywhere else.
We should explain why the microphone is needed before we ask for it.
Dark mode contrast fails on the secondary buttons at the moment.
Every icon needs a text label; the icon-only row tested badly.
Animation stays under two hundred milliseconds or it feels sluggish.
We are not shipping the illustration set until legal clears the licence.
Accessibility review happens before the beta, not after it.

meetings.title: Vendor negotiation
segments: Their first quote came in at ninety thousand for the year.
We have leverage because our contract renews before their quarter ends.
Legal flagged the auto-renewal clause and wants it struck.
If they will not move on price, we walk and self-host for six months.
The migration would cost us about three engineer-weeks.
I have a call with their account team on Wednesday morning.
Do not mention the competing quote until they put something in writing.
We need a decision before the board meeting in two weeks.
